newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris police cycle patrol back after 13 years.
newsitem.headline: Paris police cycle patrol back after 13 years.

text.p: "Swallows", unsighted in Paris streets and parks for 13 years, were back on Monday in new plumage but greatly reduced numbers.

The police bicycle patrol unit, which won its nickname for the flapping black capes that the original participants wore, has been revived as part of a new, ecologically minded effort to make officers more accessible.
Twenty-four officers in dark blue uniforms ride blue mountain bikes with flashy red spokes, much different from the ponderous black cycles of their predecessors.
The "swallows" numbered 5,000 in the 1950s, an icon of French life immortalised in dozens of films. They were overtaken by moped-mounted police from 1984.

The new unit will patrol the Boulogne and Vincennes woods on the fringes of Paris as well as pedestrian areas by the river Seine. Some mounted on quicker motorcycles will help keep cycle paths clear across the city.
"This will allow more contact with people because (police) will no longer be shut inside their cars," said Christine Bousch, a member of the new unit.
